text: Step 1: \(p\)-class. \(P_2=\gamma_2P^p=\gamma_2\), as \(P/\gamma_2\) is elementary. For \(a,b\in P\), \([a,b]^p\equiv[a^p,b]\equiv1\pmod{\gamma_3}\) since \(a^p\in\gamma_2\); so \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is elementary, \(P_3=[\gamma_2,P]\gamma_2^p=\gamma_3\) and \(P_4=\gamma_4\gamma_3^p=1\). Hence \(P\) has \(p\)-class \(3\), its nucleus is \(N=P_4(P^*)\), and \(P\) is nonterminal if and only if \(N\ne1\), if and only if \(P\) has an immediate descendant of step size \(1\) [OBr90].

Lemma. \(P\) is nonterminal if and only if there is a group \(Q\) with a central subgroup \(\langle z\rangle\) of order \(p\) such that \(Q/\langle z\rangle\cong P\) and \(\gamma_4(Q)\ne1\). For every immediate descendant \(Q\) of step size \(1\), \(P_4(Q)=\gamma_4(Q)=\langle z\rangle\), \(\gamma_5(Q)=1\), \(Q''=1\), and \(\gamma_3(Q)\) is elementary abelian of order \(p^2\).

Proof. Let \(Q\) be an immediate descendant of step size \(1\): \(P_4(Q)=\langle z\rangle\) has order \(p\) and \(Q/\langle z\rangle\cong P\). As \(P_3(Q)\) maps onto \(P_3(P)=\gamma_3(P)\), \(P_3(Q)=\gamma_3(Q)\langle z\rangle\) and \(P_4(Q)=\gamma_4(Q)\gamma_3(Q)^p\); also \(\gamma_5(Q)\le P_5(Q)=1\). For \(\ell\in\gamma_2(Q)\) and \(x\in Q\), \([\ell^p,x]=[\ell,x]^p\) since \([\ell,x,\ell]\in\gamma_5(Q)=1\), and \(\ell^p\in P_3(Q)\), so \([\ell,x]^p\in\gamma_4(Q)\). Hence \(\gamma_3(Q)/\gamma_4(Q)\) has exponent \(p\) and \(\langle z\rangle=P_4(Q)=\gamma_4(Q)\). So \(Q\) has class \(4\), its factors \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) and \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\) are those of \(P\), and Lemma 6.3 gives \(Q''=1\). For \(\ell\in\gamma_2(Q)\), \(y\in Q\) and \(c=[\ell,y]\), the element \([c,y]\) is central, so \([\ell,y^p]=c^p[c,y]^{\binom p2}=c^p\); and \(y^p\in\gamma_2(Q)\) (its image lies in \(\gamma_2(P)\), and \(z\in\gamma_2(Q)\)), so \([\ell,y^p]=1\). Since \(\gamma_3(Q)\le\gamma_2(Q)\) is abelian and generated by such \(c\), it has exponent \(p\), and its order is \(p\,|\gamma_3(P)|=p^2\).

Conversely, let \(Q\) be as in the statement. \(\gamma_4(Q)\) maps into \(\gamma_4(P)=1\), so \(\gamma_4(Q)=\langle z\rangle\). The image of \(P_4(Q)\ge\gamma_4(Q)\) in \(P\) is \(P_4(P)=1\), so \(P_4(Q)=\langle z\rangle\) and \(P_5(Q)=[\langle z\rangle,Q]\langle z\rangle^p=1\). As \(z\in\gamma_2(Q)\le\Phi(Q)\), \(d(Q)=d(P)\), so \(Q\) is an immediate descendant of \(P\) [OBr90].

Step 4: (N4) is necessary. Let \(Q\) be as in Lemma C.1, and keep the names \(x_i,u,v,w\) for fixed preimages. The group \(A=\gamma_2(Q)=\langle u,v,w,z\rangle\) is abelian; we write it additively and put \(D_xa=[a,x]=a^x-a\) for \(x\in Q\). Each \(D_x\) is an endomorphism of \(A\). We have \(D_xD_y=D_yD_x\), since \(xy=yx[x,y]\) and \([x,y]\in A\) acts trivially on \(A\). Every product of three \(D\)'s vanishes, since \([A,Q,Q,Q]\le\gamma_5(Q)=1\). For some \(\tau_{ij},\rho_i,\eta_i,\sigma_i,\mu_u,\mu_v\in\mathbb F_p\), \[[x_i,x_j]=\omega_1(i,j)u+\omega_2(i,j)v+\omega_3(i,j)w+\tau_{ij}z,\qquad x_i^p=\alpha_iv+\beta_iw+\rho_iz,\] \[D_{x_i}u=f_iw+\sigma_iz,\quad D_{x_i}v=\eta_iz,\quad D_{x_i}w=cf_iz,\] \[pu=\mu_uz,\quad pv=\mu_vz,\quad pw=0,\] by Step 2 and Lemma C.1.

(J): put \(a=[x,y]\in A\) in the Hall–Witt identity \[[x,y^{-1},t]^y\,[y,t^{-1},x]^t\,[t,x^{-1},y]^x=1.\] Then \([x,y^{-1}]=(a^{-1})^{y^{-1}}=-(1-D_y+D_y^2)a\), and, dropping products of three \(D\)'s, \[[x,y^{-1},t]^y=(1+D_y)D_t(-a+D_ya)=-D_ta=-[x,y,t].\] So \([x,y,t]+[y,t,x]+[t,x,y]=0\) holds exactly in \(Q\). For \((x,y,t)=(x_i,x_j,x_k)\), \[[x_i,x_j,x_k]=D_{x_k}[x_i,x_j]=\omega_1(i,j)(f_kw+\sigma_kz)+\bigl(\omega_2(i,j)\eta_k+c\,\omega_3(i,j)f_k\bigr)z.\] The \(w\)-component of the cyclic sum vanishes already in \(P\); the \(z\)-component is (J). (E): let \(x=x_j\), \(y=x_i\) and \(a=[x,y]\). On the one hand \((x^p)^y=x^p+D_yx^p=x^p+(\alpha_j\eta_i+c\beta_jf_i)z\). On the other hand \[(x^p)^y=(xa)^p=x^p+\sum_{m=0}^{p-1}(1+D_x)^ma=x^p+pa+\tbinom p2D_xa+\tbinom p3D_x^2a.\] Here \(D_xa\in\gamma_3(Q)\) has exponent \(p\), \(pa=(\mu_u\omega_1(j,i)+\mu_v\omega_2(j,i))z\), \(D_x^2a=c\,f_j^2\,\omega_1(j,i)z\), and \(\binom p3\equiv\varepsilon_p\pmod p\). Comparing and using \(\omega_r(j,i)=-\omega_r(i,j)\) gives (E) (for \(i=j\), \(a=0\) and (E) says \([x_j^p,x_j]=1\)). Dividing by \(c\) gives a solution with \(c=1\).

Modulo \(z\) this is the presentation of Step 3. A pc-presentation is consistent if and only if the following test words collect to the same normal form [Sim94, Ch. 9], [VL84]: for generators \(g_k>g_j>g_i\), \((g_kg_j)g_i=g_k(g_jg_i)\), \((g_j^p)g_i=g_j^{p-1}(g_jg_i)\), \(g_j(g_i^p)=(g_jg_i)g_i^{p-1}\), and \((g_i^p)g_i=g_i(g_i^p)\). All of them hold modulo \(z\), so each test compares exponents of \(z\), computed by collection from the defining relations alone. Let \(A=\langle u,v,w,zangle\), which is abelian by the relations. Conjugation by \(x_i\), as the relations give it on \(u,v,w,z\), maps them into \(A\) and respects the power relations of \(A\) (this is the content of the tests \((\ell^p)x_i\), checked below), so it induces an endomorphism \(1+D_i\) of \(A\). Let \(a_{kj}\) be the right-hand word for \([x_k,x_j]\), \(k>j\). Then \[(x_kx_j)x_i=x_ix_jx_k igl[(1+D_k)a_{ji}+a_{ki}+(1+D_i)a_{kj} igr],\] \[x_k(x_jx_i)=x_ix_jx_k igl[a_{kj}+(1+D_j)a_{ki}+a_{ji} igr],\] and the difference is \(D_ka_{ji}+D_ia_{kj}-D_ja_{ki}=-J(i,j,k)\,z\), its \(w\)-component vanishing by the identity in \(P\). The power tests repeat the computation of \((x_ja)^p\) in Step 4, which uses only the relations: \((x_j^p)x_i\) and \(x_j(x_i^p)\) (\(j>i\)) give \(\pm E(i,j)z\) and \(\pm E(j,i)z\), and \((x_i^p)x_i\) gives \(E(i,i)z\). For \(\ell\in\{u,v,w\}\), the test \((\ell,x_j,x_i)\) is the Jacobi identity with \(\ell\): it gives \((f_j\,cf_i-f_i\,cf_j)z=0\) for \(\ell=u\), and \(0\) for \(\ell=v,w\). The tests \((\ell^p)x_i\) and \(\ell(x_i^p)\) hold because \(p\,D_i\ell=0\) and \((1+D_i)^p\ell=\ell\), as \(pw=pz=0\), \(D_i^3=0\) and \(p\mid inom p2\). The remaining tests, \((\ell,\ell',x_i)\) with \(\ell,\ell'\in\{u,v,w,z\}\) and those involving \(z\), hold trivially: the images of \(u,v,w,z\) under conjugation by \(x_i\) lie in the abelian group \(A\), and \(z\) is central.
